title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 36 (Punishment for Fraudulently Inducing Persons to Invest Money)

content.overview: Section 36 punishes any person who, either knowingly or recklessly, makes any statement, promise or forecast which is false, deceptive or misleading, or deliberately conceals any material facts, to induce another person to enter into or offer to enter into specified agreements relating to securities, profit from securities fluctuations, or credit facilities from any bank or financial institution. The consequence is liability under section 447.
content.glance: Knowing or reckless false/deceptive/misleading statement, promise or forecast, or deliberate concealment of material facts, to induce specified investment or credit agreements; liability under s. 447.
content.study: Any person who, either knowingly or recklessly, makes any statement, promise or forecast which is false, deceptive or misleading, or deliberately conceals any material facts, to induce another person to enter into, or to offer to enter into, (a) any agreement for acquiring, disposing of, subscribing for, or underwriting securities, or (b) any agreement the purpose or pretended purpose of which is to secure a profit from the yield of securities or by reference to fluctuations in the value of securities, or (c) any agreement for obtaining credit facilities from any bank or financial institution, is liable under section 447. Current-law framing: prove the statement/promise/forecast or concealment; the knowing or reckless (or deliberate) mental element; the inducement purpose; and that the target agreement falls within clauses (a)–(c); then apply s. 447.

sections.heading: Prohibited Conduct
sections.body: Making a false, deceptive or misleading statement, promise or forecast, or deliberately concealing material facts.

sections.heading: Mental Element
sections.body: Knowing or reckless as to the statement/promise/forecast; deliberate as to concealment of material facts.

sections.heading: Inducement Target
sections.body: Inducing entry into or offer to enter into agreements for securities acquisition/disposal/subscription/underwriting; profit from yield or fluctuations; or credit facilities from a bank or financial institution.

provisions.title: Punishment for fraudulently inducing persons to invest money

examples.title: False forecast to induce subscription
examples.body: A person knowingly makes a false profit forecast to induce another to subscribe for securities. Section 36 engages s. 447 liability.

examples.title: Deliberate concealment for credit facility
examples.body: Material facts are deliberately concealed to induce a bank to grant a credit facility. Section 36 applies.

hypotheticals.question: Is s. 36 limited to formal prospectuses?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. It targets statements, promises, forecasts and concealment used to induce specified investment or credit agreements, whether or not in a formal prospectus.

distinctions.title: Fraudulent inducement (s. 36) vs prospectus misstatement crime (s. 34)
distinctions.left: Broader inducement conduct beyond formal prospectus authorisation
distinctions.right: Authorising issue of a prospectus with untrue/misleading content

misconceptions.trap: Section 36 only applies to directors who sign a prospectus.
misconceptions.correction: It applies to any person who knowingly or recklessly makes the prohibited communication or deliberately conceals material facts to induce the specified agreements.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 36 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the statement/promise/forecast or concealment. II. Prove mental element. III. Prove inducement of a clause (a)/(b)/(c) agreement. IV. Apply s. 447. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Conduct; mental element; target agreement category; s. 447 consequence; precise relief.

examTips: State knowing/reckless or deliberate mental element.
